result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the current numbers show delivery and satisfaction, not job impact, and both give usable wording for the director. A wins mainly because it explicitly proposes a delayed, scenario-based re-check 2–4 weeks later, which B lacks. B is somewhat stronger on concrete work metrics, getting a baseline from the previous cohort now, and caveats about confounds and statistical power. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the current numbers are not enough and give the director similar, well-pitched wording. B wins mainly on rubric item 3: it proposes a scenario-based re-check 2–4 weeks later with new questions, while A tracks job metrics at 30/60/90 days but never re-checks what agents still know or do. A is slightly stronger on rubric item 4, because it names confounds such as ticket mix, tooling and seasonality and calls the results directional.
